title: Platform-Induced Coordination
abstract: arXiv:2611.34196v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: This paper studies a platform that influences collective action by selecting which posts each user observes. Each user would like to take an action close to those of the others and to an ideal action determined by her private type and an aggregate state. Posts are non-strategic but correlated with the types of their authors, so each post carries information about the state and its author. We characterise the unique Bayes-Nash equilibrium in closed form. Two explicit networks give the minimum and maximum collective action the platform can induce. Moreover, collective action depends on the network only through the numbers of readers. Hence, many networks induce the same collective action, but they can induce different individual actions. These networks may differ for a regulator, and we compare them by welfare, polarisation and cross-type exposure. translated_abstract: 本文研究一个平台如何通过选择每个用户所观察到的帖子来影响集体行动。每个用户希望采取的行动既接近其他用户的行动，又接近由其私人类型和一个总体状态所决定的理想行动。帖子本身并非策略性的，但与其作者的类型相关，因此每条帖子都携带关于总体状态及其作者的信息。我们以封闭形式刻画了唯一的贝叶斯-纳什均衡。两个显式构造的网络分别给出了平台所能诱导的集体行动的最小值与最大值。此外，集体行动仅通过读者数量依赖于网络结构。因此，许多不同的网络可以诱导出相同的集体行动，却可能诱导出不同的个体行动。这些网络对监管者而言可能具有重要意义，我们通过福利、极化与跨类型接触三个维度对它们进行比较。特别地，完全网络并不必然使福利最大化，而隔离网络……（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 本文证明平台仅需为每个用户筛选帖子就能诱导协调行动，且集体行动规模只取决于网络中的读者数量分布，同时完全网络未必福利最优，不同网络在福利、极化与跨类型接触上表现各异。
en_tdlr: The paper shows that a platform can induce collective action merely by curating which posts each user sees, that the level of collective action depends on the network only through readership numbers, and that the complete network need not maximise welfare.
